facts.statement: The extinct sauropod dinosaur Vahiny means "traveller" in Malagasy and is known from the Late Cretaceous Maevarano Formation in northwestern Madagascar.
facts.quote: Vahiny (meaning "traveller" in Malagasy) is an extinct genus of titanosaur sauropod dinosaur known from the Late Cretaceous of the Maevarano Formation, northwestern Madagascar.

facts.statement: Kristina Curry Rogers and Jeffrey A. Wilson first described and named the genus Vahiny and its type species Vahiny depereti in 2014.
facts.quote: Vahiny was first described and named by Kristina Curry Rogers and Jeffrey A. Wilson in 2014 and the type species is Vahiny depereti.

facts.statement: Vahiny is most similar to the Late Cretaceous Indian dinosaur Jainosaurus and shares similarities with the South American taxa Muyelensaurus and Pitekunsaurus.
facts.quote: Vahiny is most similar to Jainosaurus from the Late Cretaceous of India, and bears similarities to the South American taxa Muyelensaurus and Pitekunsaurus.

facts.statement: Vahiny lived in a semiarid coastal floodplain environment that experienced distinct wet and dry seasons.
facts.quote: Vahiny lived in what was once a semiarid coastal floodplain. This area experienced distinct wet and dry seasons.

facts.statement: Vahiny is classified within the unranked family Titanosauria.
Vahiny lived during the Late Cretaceous, between 70 and 66 million years ago in the Maastrichtian stage.
facts.quote: que vivó a finales del período Cretácico, entre 70 a 66 millones de años durante el Maastrichtiense

facts.statement: The parent group for the genus Vahiny is Lithostrotia.
The time range for Vahiny is the Maastrichtian, from 72.2 to 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Maastrichtian (72.2 to 66 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Vahiny is distinguished from other titanosaurs by specific characteristics of its braincase, such as the basal tubera, basipterygoid processes, parasphenoid, and cranial nerve foramina.
rejected.quote: Vahiny is distinguished from other titanosaurs by characteristics of its braincase, including the basal tubera, basipterygoid processes, parasphenoid and cranial nerve foramina.

rejected.statement: As a sauropod, Vahiny was a herbivore that used its long neck to browse on vegetation like conifers, cycads, and early flowering plants.
rejected.quote: As a sauropod, Vahiny was a herbivore. It would have used its long neck to browse on vegetation, possibly feeding on a variety of plants available in its habitat, such as conifers, cycads, and early flowering plants.
